rules: total cash, earmarked funds and unallocated cash are three separate quantities: a contribution raises the earmark and lowers unallocated cash without reducing total cash; the due expense reduces total cash and releases its earmark exactly once
a recorded allocation is journalled money set aside, never a planned one; time passing over a contribution date proves nothing was saved

final-contribution-adjustment-v1: every contribution date carries the same whole minor-unit amount and the final date absorbs the remainder, so the scheduled contributions sum to the shortfall exactly

a proposal reports the amount and date that were observed and names what is missing; it never asks for a guessed figure, and it never replaces the data-derived irregular allowance — only a confirmed fund with a sourced amount and due date does that, and only for its own matching amount

recurrence is known only where a schedule was actually recorded; repeated observations of a similar expense are evidence of repetition, never proof of an annual pattern, and one isolated purchase is proof of nothing
a due-now or overdue expense stays an obligation: the fund reports an immediate funding requirement instead of being refused
an allocation sits within liquid cash; one that exceeds the available unallocated cash is kept and warned about, never trimmed to fit
scheduling contributions moves no cash on any day, so a schedule can never make an insolvent cash path solvent
